items.meaning_mnemonic: At Grandma Kane's shrine, three fence posts lean out of the moss at different heights. A groundskeeper strings one rope low for the toddlers, one higher for the parents, one higher still for the grandparents, refusing to leave until all three cross the same posts. The tangle reads as one family: three generations roped to the same ground.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei, hand up before anyone asks, elbows in to fix the groundskeeper's ropes and gets both ankles lassoed for it. She yanks free, smooths her uniform, and announces the fix in one clipped syllable that sounds exactly like you'd <reading>say</reading> it: <reading>せい</reading>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: On orientation day, the new hires drive the <radical>earth</radical> signpost into the ground behind Grandma Kane's shrine, right beside the stone <radical>altar</radical> where offerings sit out for everyone to see. items.description: 社 originally named the local earth god's shrine — the altar raised on a patch of claimed ground for a village's protector spirit. The word later stretched to cover any group organized around a shared institution, which is why it equally means a shrine and a company: the modern sense kept the idea of a formal body bound to a place, not the religious content.

items.description: 者 almost never stands alone as a word; it works as a suffix stitched onto a verb or field to name whoever does it, much the way English -er turns 'teach' into 'teacher'. items.mnemonic_text: The sun (日) already up over the ground (十): early.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone has scratched the <radical>ten</radical> mark into the dirt — two matchsticks crossed, the tally you cut when you've counted both hands — and stood it upright like a fencepost. Behind it the <radical>sun</radical>, that window with a bar in it, comes climbing up to start a new <radical>day</radical> and clears the top of the post before you've counted anywhere near ten. It's up hours ahead of your alarm, and now everything you do today has to be fast: early, fast.

items.description: Means "early" or "fast," and shows up in everyday words about time and speed like 早い (early/fast) and 早く (quickly).

items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture 活 as one scene: fizzing splashes flung sideways above a shape jerking back to life below. A commuter has fainted onto the floor of Koichi's konbini, and the clerk empties an energy drink over him. He sits bolt upright mid-gasp, tapping his foot before his eyes open — that fizzing jolt is 活: lively, revived, helped back onto his feet.
items.reading_mnemonic: The commuter jolts upright and sneezes so hard he headbutts the shelf — a violent <reading>ka-choo</reading> that comes out sounding exactly like <reading>かつ</reading>, onigiri raining down around him. Koichi just restocks the shelf and waits for the next customer to keel over the same way.
